content:
Marissa Cole: Question for the group: do we want Console to *block* creating an experiment on a route that already has an active experiment? Or allow “overlapping experiments” with some priority/ordering?

Marissa Cole: Seeing this come up in beta onboarding. Customers ask “can I run A/B on model *and* A/B on caching policy” on the same endpoint.

Jada Williams: From policy engine POV, overlapping experiments is a footgun unless we define a deterministic precedence rule (and stickiness semantics get weird).

Jada Williams: If two experiments both claim the same route, are we doing nested bucketing? multiply variants? priority wins? If priority wins, the “losing” experiment gets 0 traffic silently unless we surface it.

Dylan Brooks: +1. Also our results views assume attribution {route, experiment_id, variant}. If two experiments fire on the same request we either emit 2 attributions (cardinality + ambiguity) or choose one.

Chloe Martin: Control plane validation is easy to enforce: unique active experiment per route_id. But we need to define what “route_id” means (templated path vs raw path). We already normalize to route template in config.

Jordan Lee: Deterministic assignment: if we allowed overlaps with priority, evaluation order must be stable across regions + versions. That’s doable but adds state. Also if someone edits priority, users get remapped (breaking “stickiness”).

Kenji Nakamura: UX-wise, allowing overlap means we need a UI for priority + explaining outcomes. That’s a lot of cognitive load for the create flow.

Kenji Nakamura: If we block, we can make it super explicit: “Only one active experiment per route. Stop the existing one first.”

Tessa Morgan: Agree. It’s also easier to communicate guardrails/blast radius: one experiment owns the route’s traffic split.

Marissa Cole: Blocking for GA feels safer, but do we need an “override” for internal / advanced users?

Ethan Park: Operationally, overlapping configs will be a source of support tickets (“why is my experiment not getting traffic”). Also increases config propagation churn.

Dylan Brooks: Proposed policy: prevent *active* overlap. Maybe allow creating a DRAFT experiment even if there’s an active one, but you can’t start it until the other is stopped.

Chloe Martin: That seems good. Validation rules:
- You can save DRAFT with overlapping route
- Starting (transition DRAFT->RUNNING) fails if any RUNNING experiment claims same route_id
- Also block if there’s a STOPPING state? depends on semantics

Jada Williams: STOPPING (drain) complicates. But if STOPPING still routes traffic, we should treat it as active for conflict purposes.

Jordan Lee: +1. Router still needs a single decision source.

Marissa Cole: What about PAUSED? (if we add later)

Jada Williams: Same as active, IMO. If it can be resumed without reconfig, it should still “own” the route to avoid surprise.

Marcus Lin: From security/audit side: overlap with priority = more change surface area and harder to reason about who changed what caused traffic shifts. Blocking is cleaner for change control.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: RBAC angle: if we allow overlap, you could create a lower-priority experiment that’s inert but later bump priority if you have edit permissions. That’s basically a second control path. Prefer single owner to reduce privilege confusion.

Kenji Nakamura: Copy draft for the wizard validation state:
“Another experiment is already running on this route ({{existing_experiment_name}}). Stop it before starting a new experiment. You can still save this experiment as a draft.”

Tessa Morgan: +1, and add a link to the existing experiment details page.

Dylan Brooks: We should also add a more direct error on start:
`Cannot start experiment: route {{route_id}} already has active experiment {{experiment_id}} (state=RUNNING).`

Chloe Martin: For UI we can map that to a banner + inline route field error.

Marissa Cole: Do we want a “Stop existing & start new” CTA? Might be too risky.

Jada Williams: Please no one-click swap for now. Too easy to accidentally cut over traffic.

Jordan Lee: Also swapping changes bucketing and can cause users to flip variants across experiments. It’s a big behavior change.

Kenji Nakamura: Alternative (less scary) CTA could be “View existing experiment” and “Duplicate configuration”.

Dylan Brooks: Another thought: what about allowing overlap only if experiments have mutually exclusive eligibility rules (e.g., header matches)?

Ethan Park: That’s basically a rules engine. Hard to validate reliably and would be error prone.

Marissa Cole: Yeah, feels like a v2 feature (segment-based experiments).

Chloe Martin: Implementation plan (Console + API):
- Add conflict check in start endpoint
- Add warning in create wizard if route overlaps an existing active experiment (non-blocking for saving draft)
- In list/details, show “Conflicts: 1 active experiment on this route” if draft overlaps

Dylan Brooks: Also add docs line: “One active experiment per route. If you need multiple changes, encode them as variants within one experiment (A/B/n).”

Tessa Morgan: For UX copy on the route picker, we can show a pill: “In use by {{exp}}” next to the route.

Kenji Nakamura: Yes. That’s consistent with other Console patterns.

Marissa Cole: Any objections to *blocking start* when overlap exists (RUNNING/STOPPING) + allowing draft save?

Jada Williams: No objection. That’s the safest baseline.

Jordan Lee: Works for determinism. :thumbsup:

Kaitlyn Nguyen: :thumbsup: from authz perspective.

Marcus Lin: :thumbsup:

Dylan Brooks: Cool. I’ll add to the validation edge cases doc + make sure we align with the state machine.

Chloe Martin: I’ll handle API error shape so Console can render nice copy.

Marissa Cole: Great. Decision summary:
- GA: enforce at most 1 active experiment per route_id
- Drafts may overlap but cannot be started until the active experiment is stopped
- Console will show warning copy + link to existing experiment

Tessa Morgan: Can someone paste the final copy into the UX spec section? I’ll make sure it’s consistent with tone.

Kenji Nakamura: On it. Will drop a snippet in the spec + tag @Tessa.

Dylan Brooks: (Adding note) We should also monitor “variant 0 traffic” / “0 traffic to experiment” metrics to catch cases where conflict slips through due to route_id normalization mismatch.

Jada Williams: Yep. And we should log conflict detection decisions in audit trail when start fails (actor, route_id, conflicting experiment_id).

Marissa Cole: Perfect. Thanks all.
